symptoms: Small brown to black spots on leaves
Spots often have concentric rings forming a 'target-like' pattern
Lesions enlarge and may merge together
Leaf yellowing and premature leaf drop
Severe infections can reduce plant growth and yield
favorable_conditions: High humidity or prolonged leaf wetness
disease_cycle: The fungus survives in infected crop residues, seeds, and weeds
Spores are produced on infected tissues
Spores spread through wind, rain splash, irrigation water, and tools
Infection occurs when spores land on wet leaves
Multiple infection cycles can occur during a growing season
monitoring: Inspect leaves regularly for brown or black spots
Look for concentric ring patterns on lesions
Monitor humidity and temperature conditions favorable to the disease

cultural: Use certified disease-free seeds and planting materials
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
Remove and destroy infected plant debris after harvest
Improve air circulation by proper plant spacing and pruning
chemical: Apply protective fungicides such as Mancozeb
Copper-based fungicides can help reduce disease spread
Rotate fungicides with different FRAC groups to avoid resistance
biological: Use biological control agents such as Bacillus subtilis formulations
Encourage beneficial microorganisms that suppress fungal pathogens

impact.crop_loss: Moderate to severe depending on environmental conditions and crop susceptibility
impact.economic_importance: Common disease in many vegetable crops worldwide that can significantly reduce yield and quality
